summary: The six-target proof is real: both per-engine invocations produced genuine device artifacts, real provider records (aborted stop turns with 71-145 deltas, nonexistent-model rejections, restore-verification responses), one candidate SHA across identical manifest digests, distinct run ids, clean teardowns, and honest RED plus a flake ledger; typecheck, scoped biome (direct binary — the pnpm exec spawn failure is the documented local artifact), and the accumulated-evidence vitest suite all pass under my independent re-run, and my fresh uniwind rerun drove both proof pipelines green on the reserved devices before dying to the documented port-4000 teardown race in the ORI-RN-004-owned seam (exit 1, fail-closed). The session-scoping and completed_before_stop rederivations are legitimate oracle corrections I verified against the raw journals. But AC-1 cannot be approved: this cycle changed the native follow-up-bubble lookup to 'For request' — a wording only the web session sends and that appears zero times in native evidence — making latest_user_message_nonce_occurrences structurally 0 (a weakened assertion), and the truncation-tolerant recall fallback matches marker text in user bubbles rather than the follow-up answer, with a degenerate anchor on uniwind-ios where all turn records share one journal timestamp. Two targeted fixes in live-example-proof.ts (match the drivers' real 'What marker' wording across observer samples; require answer-shaped anchored matches) restore AC-1's discriminating power without touching any other gate.
